speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. I understand you have been experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination. To help me understand your condition better, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The relief of discomfort after voiding and painful intercourse are significant findings. Have you noticed any blood in your urine or a burning sensation specifically during urination?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis (Painful Bladder Syndrome).

Based on your 5-month history of bladder pain relieved by voiding, significant urinary frequency, and dyspareunia (painful intercourse), combined with the lack of response to NSAIDs and absence of urinary retention or infection symptoms, the clinical picture strongly suggests interstitial cystitis.
